author: jackclarkSF
text: @NPCollapse So I'm saying "frontier ban regimes as currently configured, though well intentioned, are politically infeasible and will be hacked around in numerous ways, and people are discounting many other ideas which also need to be worked on to make such bans effective"

author: jackclarkSF
text: @NPCollapse So just to be agonizingly clear, if someone took away all GPUs from all labs id say "that's fine but if you don't build public compute infrastructure I guarantee you that energy will go into weaponizing all the hardware you didn't control and you have to change that incentive"

author: jackclarkSF
text: @NPCollapse Yeah, I don't disagree. A world where we can push a button and stop larger compute things being built and all focus on safety for a while is good. I'm not sure also the compute control stuff gets you that and there are ways to game it, so need effort on other ideas also.

author: jackclarkSF
text: My main thoughts are that policy which looks like picking winners is basically bad policy, and compute controls (and related ideas like 'licensing') have this problem. They feel very politically difficult. This is why I spend a lot of time on stuff like National Research Clouds

author: jackclarkSF
text: Will write something longer, but if best ideas for AI policy involve depriving people of the 'means of production' of AI (e.g H100s), then you don't have a hugely viable policy. (I 100% am not criticizing @Simeon_Cps here; his tweet highlights how difficult the situation is).

author: jackclarkSF
text: In a very real sense, writing feels like a form of cognitive 'embodiment' - whether in fiction or non-fiction we are using our brain as an interface between the real and the ethereal and we produce these text-based artifacts as ways to ground the two worlds together.

author: jackclarkSF
text: I write short stories because they help me process the great mystery that is the world and convert it into stories and things I can allow my mind to live inside and crawl over. Whenever I write I am desperately trying to understand the world and my place within it.

author: jackclarkSF
text: One gnawing worry I have about the rise of LLMs is that, for me, writing IS thinking. One reason I spend so much time writing my newsletter each week is I haven't figured out a better way to think about AI than to sit down and write about it regularly.

author: jackclarkSF
text: One core production input for AI systems is labelled data. The implications of us crossing the Rubicon of systems being able to generate good quality data that doesn't exhibit some pathological garbage in, garbage out failure mode are profound. And it is beginning to happen!

author: jackclarkSF
text: Something that will further compound acceleration of AI research is that models are now better and cheaper than humans at data generation and classification tasks - this already true for some cases (eg Facebooks Segment Anything model, and GPT-4 for some labeling).

author: jackclarkSF
text: A mental model I have of AI is it was roughly ~linear progress from 1960s-2010, then exponential 2010-2020s, then has started to display 'compounding exponential' properties in 2021/22 onwards. In other words, next few years will yield progress that intuitively feels nuts.

author: jackclarkSF
text: AI promises to be one of the most transformative classes of technology ever developed (potentially, the most transformative!) so it's crazy to me that in the Western World we are basically assigning one class of org (private sector companies) the ability to develop this.

author: jackclarkSF
text: Also, to be clear - I like companies! Companies can do useful things. I am a co-founder of a company and my goal is for us to do useful things! But I am aware companies have various incentives they operate in and there are other organizational structures with diff incentives.

author: jackclarkSF
text: There will of course be exceptions and some companies will release stuff. But this isn't going to get us many of the benefits of the magic of contemporary AI. We're surrendering our own culture and our identity to the logic of markets. I am aghast at this. And you should be too.

author: jackclarkSF
text: Modern AI development highlights the tragedy of letting the private sector lead AI invention - the future is here but it's mostly inaccessible due to corporations afraid of PR&Policy risks. (This thought sparked by Google not releasing its music models, but trend is general). https://t.co/wsRWJRFcGW
